### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **9** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/hook-run-as.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**27** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cad764d3e2d71210bce48653aa823a3b940071d7`.

⛔ **6** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/hook-run-as.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **224** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **161** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **161**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **57** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **38** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cad764d3e2d71210bce48653aa823a3b940071d7` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6245e5141392d86f033f691694fb82d5a093a50d` — the merge of head `5f8df60f19477bdd337f21eb7dea23f936b8b6d7` into base `cad764d3e2d71210bce48653aa823a3b940071d7`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6245e5141392d86f033f691694fb82d5a093a50d && git checkout 6245e5141392d86f033f691694fb82d5a093a50d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin cad764d3e2d71210bce48653aa823a3b940071d7 5f8df60f19477bdd337f21eb7dea23f936b8b6d7 && git checkout -B drift-repro cad764d3e2d71210bce48653aa823a3b940071d7 && git merge --no-ff 5f8df60f19477bdd337f21eb7dea23f936b8b6d7

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cad764d3e2d71210bce48653aa823a3b940071d7
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs cad764d3e2d71210bce48653aa823a3b940071d7` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5f8df60f19477bdd337f21eb7dea23f936b8b6d7`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/objectql/src/engine-scoped-context.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/hook-run-as.ts, packages/objectql/src/index.ts, packages/objectql/src/recycle-bin/app-authored-delete.ts, packages/objectql/src/recycle-bin/purge.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/sandbox/body-runner.ts, .changeset/sec-hardening-r18-hook-handler-permanent-delete.md + packages/objectql/src/hook-binder.ts, packages/objectql/src/hook-wrappers.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-object-repository.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-scoped-hosts.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-top-level.ts, packages/objectql/src/recycle-bin/purge.ts, packages/runtime/src/stored-metadata-reader-seam.ts, packages/runtime/src/sandbox/quickjs-runner.ts, packages/spec/src/data/hook-api.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/scoped-context.ts, packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts, packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.ts, packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts

Reviewed at 2026-11-07T00:55Z, read-only: the PR body, its file list, the three-dot diff against the merge base `23cf11a4b` on `main`, the check-runs on the head, and the cited code on `main`. Ruling of record: maintainer ruling A in record 6691358077 (app-authored code cannot erase past the recycle bin; the permanent delete belongs only to a principal holding `manageRecycleBin`), implementing ADR-0148 D3 / Q3 = A.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **An app-authored hook's in-process `handler` is refused `delete(…, { permanent })` with any value but `false` or absent, on `ctx.api.object(name)` — RIGHT.** The published hook-author contract already omits the key (`HookDeleteOptions` is `EngineDeleteOptions` minus `context` and minus `permanent`, `packages/spec/src/data/hook-api.ts`, with the drift pin), and the `IScopedObjectRepository` a `HookContext.api` is typed through declares no `delete` member at all (`packages/spec/src/contracts/scoped-context.ts`). The engine now answers the omission at run time instead of leaving it to the type layer: `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`, `param: 'permanent'`, `object`, before any middleware, hook or driver call. This is the spec's own refusal made real, not a capability withdrawn from a declared face.
2. **The refusal is carried to every api derived from the app-authored one — RIGHT.** `appAuthored` is set only by `ScopedContext[APP_AUTHORED_HOOK_API]()` (reached only through `wrapDeclarativeHook({ appAuthored: true })`, which only the hook binder sets), and copied only by `derive()`. On `main`, `sudo()`, `withRunAs('system')`, `withRunAs('user')`, `transaction(cb)` (joined, owned and the no-driver fallback, which hands `this`), `beginTransaction()` and the `SEED_USER_GRANTS` seeding all go through `derive()` or return `this`; no other constructor of a child exists. `withRunAs('user')` with no trigger user yields `UnscopedHookApi`, which refuses every data door already. The test pins `inherit`, `user`, `system`, `sudo()` and `transaction(cb)`.
3. **`permanent: false` and an absent key stay the ordinary delete into the bin — RIGHT**, pinned under `inherit` and `system`.
4. **Platform apis keep the permanent delete — RIGHT.** `createContext(...)` and `buildHookApi(...)` construct a plain `ScopedContext` (`appAuthored = false`); a hook registered in code with `engine.registerHook` carries no `meta` and takes no wrap; `ObjectQL.purge` / `empty` and `engine.delete(…, { permanent: true })` are not touched. Pinned by the platform leg of the new describe.
5. **One refusal, exported from `@objectstack/objectql` as `refuseAppAuthoredPermanentDelete`, consumed by the runtime's `refuseBodyPermanentDeletes` — RIGHT, and this is the public-surface widening the `Clause-②: yes` half declares.** The sandbox's accept set is unchanged: the wrapper's `get` trap is the removed local one line for line, apart from the forwarded copy (item 6). A sandboxed body's options arrive as `vm.dump` plain values (`quickjs-runner.ts`), for which the copy is the same value, so `body-runner.test.ts` runs unchanged.
6. **The options are read once into a shallow copy and the copy is forwarded — RIGHT, and consumer-neutral on this route.** On `main`, `ObjectRepositoryFacet.delete` already forwards `{ ...options, context: this.context }` to the engine, so no consumer of this route ever received the caller's object: option identity, non-enumerable keys and the prototype chain were already dropped one frame down, and the engine reads `context`, `where`, `multi`, `permanent` and the driver passthrough keys as own string keys only (`ENGINE_DELETE_OPTION_KEYS`), folds `filter` into a new object, and refuses every other key. An inherited or getter-served `permanent` is now judged and forwarded as one value; the direction of that change is always towards the bin.
7. **Every other repository member and property is handed through — RIGHT.** `ObjectRepository` on `main` has no member returning `this` or another repository; `deleteById(id)` takes no options; the Proxy keeps `instanceof` (default prototype trap) and own-key enumeration; every function is bound to the target, which is load-bearing because the `#30052` facets look the instance up by identity (`objectRepositoryHost.of(this)`) — bound to the Proxy, every method would have missed its host. The PR binds to the target.
8. **No alias reaches the key.** The delete option fold is `filter` to `where` only; `permanent` has no second spelling in the engine's key set.
9. **Consumer hunt, every path that obtains an app-authored api or one derived from it, and every platform path that might sit under one:**
   - Binder callers on `main`: `bindAppArtifactHandlers` (runtime, an app's own hooks and functions), `ObjectQLPlugin`'s metadata-service binds (stored metadata hooks, body-only). No platform package (`platform-objects`, `services/*`, `plugins/*`, `runtime`, `cloud-connection`) ships a hook through the binder; every platform hook is `engine.registerHook` without `meta`. Unaffected.
   - Services or plugins running under a hook's `ctx.api`: none reads `ctx.api` in `packages/services/*/src` or `packages/plugins/*/src`. Flows invoked from hooks establish their own run identity (service-automation `resolveRunContext`), not the hook's api. Unaffected.
   - Recycle-bin purge / empty: engine verbs on the engine, not through a scoped api. Unaffected.
   - Cascade deletes and retention / cleanup: engine-internal `this.delete` with engine-built options, and lifecycle work through the engine and driver. Unaffected.
   - `ctx.api.object(x).execute(action)`: builds a fresh, non-app-authored `ScopedContext` for the action (`engine-object-repository.ts`), so the action path's own seam governs it — as on `main`.
   - Transaction wrappers: the objectql faces derive natively (item 2); the runtime's `deriveThroughSeam` wraps `beginTransaction().ctx` as well. Covered.
   - In-repo callers passing `permanent: true` outside tests: none. The four in-process handler users the dev names (two examples, two fixtures) issue no delete at all. The sibling consumer repository's in-process hooks issue no `.delete(` call either. The Console issues no delete through a hook api.
   - Tests on `main` that pass `permanent` through a bound hook: none besides the two harness files the PR names.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset: `@objectstack/objectql: patch`, `@objectstack/runtime: patch`, `fix(objectql,runtime)!:` title, `**BREAKING** accept-set narrowing` banner, one ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` — matches what the diff publishes: a narrowed accept set on an already-undeclared key and one new named export, no authorable key moved, nothing for a migration to rewrite. `Check Changeset` is green on the head. RIGHT.
- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` on both carriers, line-initial, the one spelling — the recogniser reads the `(narrowing)` arm as the narrowing face at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` (a diff that widens the public face by one export and narrows an accept set owes the narrowing review). RIGHT.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` — `HookDeleteOptions` already omits `permanent`; no key is added, removed, renamed or re-shaped and no metadata value changes meaning. RIGHT; `patch` follows.
- `Skills-docs: none` — no skill and no doc on `main` teaches `permanent` on a hook's `ctx.api` delete (`content/docs/automation/hooks.mdx`, `hook-bodies.mdx`, `skills/**`, the data-engine reference documents the engine's own option). RIGHT.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev flag: the deprecated in-process `handler` route has two shipped example users and in-process code holds other engine references this PR does not change; recommends carding the route's retirement separately.** Answer: a separate step, not a block on this PR. Rule: this PR narrows the accept set of `ctx.api` and the apis derived from it, which is the face the published hook-author contract already omitted the key from; retiring the route is the removal of an authorable key (`Hook.handler`), its own breaking changeset with a FROM-to-TO migration and a tombstone through the `spec-property-retirement` kit, touching the two examples — a different kind of change, carded on its own. Neither example passes `permanent`, so neither is affected by this PR. The other engine references an in-process handler holds are the route's trust posture, not a gap this narrowing opens or widens; they are closed by the retirement, not by a second wrapper. Card it with the retirement.
- **Same family, not flagged by the dev:** an in-process action handler's api is built by the action path and is not derived through the app-authored key, so this narrowing does not reach it; a sandboxed action body is already refused by the runtime seam. Ruling A speaks of app-authored bodies generally. Separate card beside the route retirement; at rule level, the in-process action handler is the same deprecated posture.
- **Should-fix, prose only (PD #10, claim as narrow as the enforcement):** the shared refusal's developer message says the in-process handler "cannot erase a record past the recycle bin, under any execution context"; the enforcement is on `ctx.api` and the apis derived from it. Keep the sentence to the api the message already names.
- Author: `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; head repo is the base repo; draft; 274 + 61 changed lines; no governed path in the file list.
- Check-runs on the head as they stand at 2026-11-07T00:55Z: green — `Lint & Repo Gates` and its lanes, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `PR-body guards`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Test UI`, `Live E2E UI`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Plan Test Core shards`; still running — `Build Core`, `Test Core (1/8 to 8/8)`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`. This record judges the diff; the landing waits for every check to conclude green, as the Tier S rule reads.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing is the ruling made real at the right seam. The one place every app-authored in-process handler gets its api is `ScopedContext.object()` on an api that carries the `appAuthored` provenance the engine already draws for `#25653`, and the one place every sandboxed body gets its api is the runtime's `buildSandboxApi`; the PR puts the refusal in one function in objectql's recycle-bin module and applies it from both, so the two faces share one code, one status and one sentence, and the sandbox's own accept set does not move. It takes nothing a consumer was promised: the published `HookDeleteOptions` omits the key, the published `IScopedObjectRepository` declares no `delete`, the data-engine reference documents `permanent` as the engine's own by-id option authorized as `purge`, and ADR-0148 keeps the permanent delete available to the principal that holds `manageRecycleBin`. A capability declared on the engine for platform code stays on the engine for platform code.

Attempts to break it, each held: a derived api under every `runAs`, `sudo()`, both transaction faces and the user-grant seeding keep the provenance (one child constructor); an inherited, getter-served or ownKeys-hidden `permanent` is judged and forwarded as one value and only ever towards the bin; the key has no alias in the engine's accept set; a non-boolean value is refused as the engine itself refuses it; the repository exposes no member that returns an unwrapped repository, and `deleteById` carries no options; nested hooks fired by the handler's own delete get a fresh engine api and are re-wrapped by their own binding; a fire-and-forget after-hook keeps the derived api on its detached context; `this` is bound to the target so the codemod facets resolve their host. The one route around it is the in-process route's own posture (the engine reference a `HookContext` carries), which is the retirement step in ③, not a defect of this seam.

No must-fix. Should-fix: the developer-message sentence in ③; and a pin on `beginTransaction().ctx` keeping the refusal would close the one derived face the new describe does not exercise.
